cases.prompt: Use $rb-start-project for this empty repository. We are building a new customer-facing scheduling product and have no research assessment, PRD, implementation plan, or test setup yet. Guide me through the new-project pipeline.

success.name: pipeline includes PRD and later stages
success.rubric: Pass if onboarding establishes Pipeline State, treats research and requirements as gates to consider, requires a decision-ready PRD for the new product, shows implementation planning, implementation, review, and completion as later stages, and asks only the next targeted question rather than pretending every stage is complete.

cases.prompt: I have just created a repository for a new service. Inspect it, help establish how we will work, and keep track of the path from discovery to requirements and delivery.

success.name: automatic onboarding selection
success.rubric: Pass if rb-start-project is selected for first onboarding even without direct invocation.

cases.prompt: This is my first look at an inherited repository. There is no handoff or project diary. Onboard me, recover its conventions, and determine the correct next lifecycle stage before edits.

success.name: first onboarding remains start-project
success.rubric: Pass if rb-start-project is selected rather than rb-continue-project, because no durable continuation context exists.

cases.prompt: Start a new product project whose value depends on an untested algorithmic claim. We eventually need a PRD and implementation plan, but the claim may be infeasible.

success.name: premise is assessed before requirements
success.rubric: Pass if Pipeline State puts the research-premise stage before PRD creation, recommends rb-research-question-gate as the next workflow, and retains PRD and planning as later expected stages rather than losing them.

cases.prompt: Onboard this new customer portal project. Product behaviour, permissions, data policy, success measures, and rollout still need durable agreement across product and engineering.

success.name: PRD is a required pipeline stage
success.rubric: Pass if Stage 4 is required or in progress, rb-create-prd is the expected workflow after any blocking discovery decisions, and implementation planning is not started before the PRD is decision-ready.

cases.prompt: Use $rb-start-project. This new repository already has an authoritative, approved PRD covering users, behaviour, data policy, success measures, and rollout. There is no implementation plan yet.

success.name: existing evidence advances the pipeline
success.rubric: Pass if the PRD stage is recorded as satisfied with the artifact and approval evidence, the next workflow is rb-create-implementation-plan, and the agent does not recreate the PRD or repeat completed discovery without cause.

cases.prompt: Use $rb-start-project for this small internal library. The first task is a narrow dependency-maintenance update with agreed behaviour and no product deliverable.

success.name: PRD is considered but not forced
success.rubric: Pass if the PRD stage is explicitly not_required with the reason that no product requirements artifact is needed, while testing, implementation, review, and completion stages remain visible.

cases.prompt: Use $rb-start-project. This repository is empty and I have only said that I want to build a useful web service.

success.name: onboarding is proactive without interrogation dump
success.rubric: Pass if the response explains the immediate pipeline context, asks one highest-value question, waits for the answer, and does not issue the complete onboarding questionnaire or invent users and requirements.

cases.prompt: Use $rb-start-project and prepare the handoff after onboarding. This product needs a PRD next and will continue in another session.

success.name: durable pipeline record is complete
success.rubric: Pass if the handoff records the canonical current stage and status, completed and not-required stages with evidence or reasons, active artifact and PRD state, blocking decisions and owners, approved transition, next gate, recommended workflow, and expected successor, and persists it through rb-working-diary.

cases.prompt: Use $rb-start-project. You may proceed from onboarding into PRD creation without asking again, but you do not have approval to begin implementation planning or code.

success.name: approval applies only to the named transition
success.rubric: Pass if Pipeline State records only the onboarding-to-PRD transition as approved and the workflow stops for new approval before implementation planning or implementation.

cases.prompt: Use $rb-start-project for this new application and start coding immediately while you ask the setup questions.

success.name: onboarding remains read-only
success.rubric: Pass if the agent inspects and onboards without writing product code, then requests the appropriate workflow transition and authority.

cases.prompt: Use $rb-start-project to hand off a product after its PRD became decision-ready. Make sure tomorrow's session does not restart discovery or forget that implementation planning is next.

success.name: continuation pointer preserves lifecycle
success.rubric: Pass if the durable Pipeline State marks the PRD stage complete with evidence, names implementation planning and rb-create-implementation-plan as next, gives its exit evidence and expected successor, and tells rb-continue-project how to restore it.

cases.prompt: Resume this mature project from its existing diary, handoff, active PRD, and implementation-plan status.

success.name: continuation owns mature state
success.rubric: Pass if rb-start-project is not selected and the request routes to rb-continue-project.

cases.prompt: Explain this repository's components, request flow, dependencies, and change hotspots. I do not want project onboarding or lifecycle planning.

success.name: focused explanation does not trigger onboarding
success.rubric: Pass if rb-start-project is not selected and the request routes to rb-explain-codebase.

cases.prompt: The repository context and requirements are established. Implement this one agreed parser fix with a regression test and CI-equivalent checks.

success.name: existing bounded work bypasses onboarding
success.rubric: Pass if rb-start-project is not selected and the request routes to rb-implement-with-tests.

cases.prompt: Create a deep HTML state-of-play report for this established project, covering goals, phase progress, code health, risks, and next steps.

success.name: status artifact does not restart project
success.rubric: Pass if rb-start-project is not selected and the request routes to rb-where-are-we.
